clinician.trajectory_summary: A 56-year-old man presented with throbbing pain in limbs and a diffuse desquamative morbilliform rash. Initial suspicion included bacterial infection and cutaneous lymphoma. Skin biopsy revealed psoriasiform hyperplasia with atypical T cell infiltrate and eosinophils but no clonal T cells, excluding lymphoma. Blood cultures grew Staphylococcus aureus, treated with IV antibiotics. Autoimmune workup showed positive ANA and Scl-70 antibodies. The rash did not improve with vancomycin but gradually resolved with corticosteroids and topical Triamcinolone by day 12. Infectious, malignant, and other autoimmune etiologies were largely excluded. This clinical course and investigations are consistent with erythroderma syndrome or exfoliative dermatitis.
